answer: Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. Written in a one long clause plus a short one register, it stays short. Work waits on the zenith until a stranger signs it off, and that signature becomes the sable of the next round. The basalt of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. The design leans on stake bond posted per identity, released only after three unrelated confirmations, no identity may audit its own recruit.
